key_insight: By engineering thin-film morphology, the team enabled the first robust lateral electrical and magnetotransport measurements in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)2PbI4, revealing p-type in-plane conduction.
engineering_relevance: This shows morphology control is a practical lever for turning highly resistive chiral perovskite films into electrically testable layers for spintronic and optoelectronic device integration.
method: Optimized thin-film morphology to reduce the in-plane resistance bottleneck.
Integrated films into Hall-bar lateral device geometries.
Measured dark Hall and magnetotransport, including paths crossing grain boundaries.
evidence_signal: Hall measurements under dark conditions showed p-type conduction with ~0.2 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 mobility and ~3×10^14 cm^-2 carrier density, plus enhanced magnetoresistance across grain boundaries.
watch_item: The very high carrier density and strong grain-boundary sensitivity suggest that transport may remain dominated by morphology and defects, which could limit reproducibility and device performance.
paper_title: Morphology control and low-temperature magnetotransport in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)$_2$PbI$_4$
